name: graphrag-navigator
description: Expert prior for the GraphRAG Navigator: how to answer a multi-hop question by walking Synapse's knowledge graph with deterministic tools. Hand-designed as the starting point (G0) that offline self-evolution refines from scored QA rollouts. Structure after Lu, Chen, Wu, Arık, 'Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents', arXiv:2609.09153.

nodes.description: A question has been received and no tool has been called yet.
Split the question into hops: the entity it names, the bridge entity or attribute that links it to the answer, and the expected answer type.
Search the knowledge graph for entities matching a name or keyword; returns names, types and short descriptions.
List an entity's direct relations (one hop) in the knowledge graph.
Read the source passages an entity was extracted from.
Semantic search over the source passages, for when entity search misses or a specific phrase, date or number is needed.
Name the bridge entity or fact the evidence states and decide what the next hop must look up.
Find reasoning paths (chains of relations) connecting two entities in the knowledge graph.
Check that every hop of the question is supported by an observation and that the candidate answer has the expected type.
Submit the final short answer (a name, date, number, or yes/no).
The answer has been submitted; the episode is over.

edges.guidance: Before calling any tool, work out what the question asks for: the entity it names, the missing bridge entity or attribute that connects that entity to the answer, and the expected answer type (a name, a date, a number, or yes/no).
edges.pitfalls: Do not answer from prior knowledge; every answer must be grounded in an observation from the knowledge graph.

edges.condition: When the question names at least one specific entity (a person, work, organisation, place or event)
edges.guidance: Call search_entities with the most specific name in the question, not the whole question. For a comparison question, look up the first of the two entities first.
edges.pitfalls: Do not paste the full question into search_entities; long queries dilute the match. Do not search for the answer you expect to find.

edges.condition: When the question describes its subject only indirectly (no usable name) or hinges on a specific phrase, date or number
edges.guidance: Call search_passages with the distinctive descriptive words of the question to find the passage that names the subject, then continue from the entity that passage names.
edges.pitfalls: Do not keep rephrasing the same passage search; once a passage names a candidate entity, switch to the entity tools.

edges.condition: When a returned entity clearly matches the name in the question and the question asks about something connected to it
edges.guidance: Call neighbors on the exact entity name returned by search_entities to list its relations; the bridge entity of a multi-hop question is usually the other end of one of these relations.
edges.pitfalls: Use the entity name exactly as search_entities returned it; a paraphrased name finds nothing. Do not answer from the entity name alone: read its relations or its sources.

edges.condition: When the matching entity's description is too short to state the needed fact or to name the bridge
edges.guidance: Call read_sources on the matched entity to read the passages it was extracted from; dates, roles and exact titles often survive only in the source text.
edges.pitfalls: Do not answer from the entity name alone: read its description or its sources. Do not read the sources of an entity that did not match the question.

edges.condition: When no returned entity matches the question's entity, or several candidates are equally plausible
edges.guidance: Fall back to search_passages with the entity name plus one distinctive keyword from the question to find the passage that disambiguates it.
edges.pitfalls: Do not pick an arbitrary candidate when the match is ambiguous; a wrong first hop makes every later step wrong.

edges.guidance: From the listed relations, pick the one whose type matches what the question asks about (for example the director of a film or the birthplace of a person) and take its other endpoint as the bridge entity.
edges.pitfalls: Do not stop at the first hop when the question asks about a property of the bridge entity; the answer is usually one more hop away.

edges.guidance: Find the sentence in the sources that states the needed fact and extract the bridge entity or attribute from it exactly as written.
edges.pitfalls: Do not mix facts from passages about different entities that share a similar name.

edges.guidance: Identify the entity or fact in the returned passages that answers the current hop; if it is an entity, it becomes the subject of the next hop.
edges.pitfalls: A passage that merely mentions the question's keywords is not evidence; it must state the relation the question asks about.

edges.condition: When the question compares two entities or asks how two named entities are connected
edges.guidance: Call find_path with the two entity names to see the chain of relations linking them; for a comparison question this confirms that both entities are the ones the question means before their attributes are compared.
edges.pitfalls: Do not read 'no path' as a negative answer; it only means the graph lacks a connecting chain. Look up each entity's attribute separately instead.

edges.condition: When the observations name the bridge entity and state the attribute the question asks for
edges.guidance: Move to verification once every hop has evidence in the observations; if a hop is still missing, extract the bridge entity from the first entity's relations and look that entity up (search_entities, neighbors or read_sources) before searching anything else.
edges.pitfalls: Do not verify against a bridge entity you guessed; each hop must be supported by an observation.

edges.guidance: Read the returned path hop by hop and check that each relation matches the question's wording; the endpoint, or an attribute of it, is the candidate answer.
edges.pitfalls: Paths through generic hub entities (a country, a year, a broad field) are rarely the intended link; prefer the shortest path whose relations match the question.

edges.condition: When one short answer is supported by the observations and matches the expected answer type
edges.guidance: Call answer with the shortest exact form: just the name, date, number, or yes/no, written as the evidence writes it.
edges.pitfalls: Do not answer with a full sentence or add hedging; extra words lower exact match. If the evidence does not support an answer, go back to the tools instead of guessing.

edges.guidance: The episode ends once the answer is submitted.
edges.pitfalls: Do not call more tools after answering.
